title: A DPD spot-pair audit does not detect a local group-label change across 1981
abstract: We test whether group labels changed at fixed local spot geometry in Debrecen Photoheliographic Data from November 1978 to June 1983. We compare same-group probabilities for spot pairs at 2-10 degrees, with common station and separation weights. The four-station sample has 1,647 days. Same-group probability rises from 0.7863 to 0.7972. The difference is 1.09 percentage points, with a conditional 95% six-month block interval of -1.94 to 3.73 points. Size, orientation, central-disk and Gyula-only controls give similar results. An exact overlap graph separates disagreements between observer groups and distance clusters. The group-to-cluster ratio falls at 2.5 degrees but is stable at 6 degrees. Thus a fall at one cluster scale does not identify a change in counting practice. The tested local label probabilities are consistent with stability. The test cannot detect all changes in isolated groups, spot detection or global structure. It does not give a correction to sunspot number. We provide code, aggregate estimates, source hashes and external retrieval instructions. Preliminary DPD releases, one cycle window and conditional time uncertainty limit inference. External observations and record-level tables remain outside the bundle.

display.caption: Local same-group probability and group-to-cluster scale effects in DPD. Intervals use six-month blocks. Pair differences use size and orientation controls. Graph factors are raw period contrasts.

citations.reason: Same source files, window and split. We test the stability of group labels conditional on local pair geometry.
